inputs.label: Senate
inputs.value: 35 races simulated · 34 D / 31 R not up

assumptions: Polls lose half their weight every 14 days; likely-voter samples receive the highest weight.

Each race starts from its 2024 presidential lean, weighted 0.913 in the House and 0.749 in the Senate, plus the incumbent's edge: in the House 2.08 pts and 60% of how far they ran ahead of the 2024 presidential result where their party already held the seat (4.6 pts elsewhere), 5.9 pts in the Senate; then moved by the national environment. Fitted on the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms (Senate: 2018 and 2022).

The national environment blends VoteHub's generic-ballot average with the one the Senate race polls imply (polls minus fundamentals), each weighted by its precision. Polls a single party sponsored count half and lean 4 pts less toward it; where they are a race's only polls, the race stays on its fundamentals.
Races with polls blend that start with their polling average by precision: an average carries 3.5 pts of error no number of polls removes, plus 6.5 pts that shrink with more and fresher polls.
Both chambers are simulated race by race: all 435 districts and the 35 Senate races, so chamber odds equal the aggregate of the race odds.
Each race margin has 7.5 pts of error, 2.9 of it shared nationally; replayed on 2018 and 2022, the own baseline scores best at 7.5.
Fundraising and candidate quality beyond incumbency are not estimated.
